neighbours.label: Suffix '-ing' ending adjectival/participial words (exacting, approving, oxidizing, adoring, nurturing, loving, caring), esp. a verb-stem plus -ing used as modifier
fire: The editor was famously exacting about grammar and returned every draft covered in red ink.
The child basked in the warm smile and approving words of her teacher after the recital.
Chlorine is one of several oxidizing agents commonly used to disinfect swimming pools and drinking water.
The puppy was smothered with kisses by her adoring new family on the very first day.
She is a loving and caring mother who gives her children a nurturing home.
He gave her a knowing look across the table and said nothing more about it.
The court was hog-tied by the exacting rules of evidence that the older judges insisted on.
Our guide offered a soothing, nurturing voice that calmed the nervous hikers on the ridge.
quiet: The editor reads every draft carefully and returns it covered in red ink by Friday.
The child smiled at the teacher after the recital and thanked her for the kind words.
Chlorine is used to disinfect swimming pools and drinking water in many towns.
The puppy was given a warm bed and a bowl of food by her new family.
She is a mother who gives her children a safe home and plenty of time.
We are walking to the market this morning and hope to buy fresh bread there.
The court follows strict rules of evidence that the older judges insist on.
Our guide has a quiet voice that calms the nervous hikers on the ridge.

notes: Label and sentences written by Claude Sonnet subagents (8 poles each) from the card text alone (prompt: haiku_labeler/prompt_l5.md); one retry on mechanical checks. Part of a 192-pole layer-5 sweep.
